title: Prove sound identity independently of MIDI program
scope: Complete sound-selection evidence for different definitions sharing one MIDI program, including opening-event authority and ordered references.
acceptance: Create two named sound definitions with the same program but distinct path/name/role; ordered and duplicate-position events must retain the selected identities through public edits and GP8 wire references.
Reorder definitions without changing event meaning and reject broken references. Use independent consumer assertions for the distinctions that consumer actually retains.
Document and test authority among the initial sound definition, explicit opening event and channel program, including conflicts; do not deduplicate definitions by program alone.
Keep Sound-event Hidden as an explicit pinned-consumer limit even though exact wire and Go reparse retain it. Reuse existing automation-detail coverage and update only residual missing evidence.
exclusions: MIDI bank work remains #51. Do not repeat #41 or broaden into proprietary RSE preservation.

resolution: Same-program sound definitions now have focused identity, public-edit, definition-reorder, broken-reference, and exact-wire regression evidence. Separate authority cases distinguish the first-definition base program, channel fallback/conflicts, and explicit opening selections. Raw pinned consumer evidence asserts retained event order, count, positions, programs, annotations and interpolation without claiming named identities that its public model discards. Existing Hidden consumer-loss coverage and legacy mix-table limits remain unchanged. Awaiting fresh review and integrated full-gate verification; the issue remains open.
